title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Resilience and Adaptation in Food Systems: Food and Nutrition Security for Those Furthest Behind programme will work in Tahoua Region, Niger. It aims to contribute to Concern Niger’s Food Systems for Food Security and WASH thematic programmes, and the goal of the grant is to build resilient food systems that prioritize food and nutrition security for the extreme poor, while promoting sustainable management of natural resources. The programme will support over 71,925 people living in households with children under five, pregnant and lactating mothers, households with disabled members, people living with HIV, female headed households. This will be done through sustainable, conflict-sensitive and risk-based natural resource management that support stable food production, increased crop diversification for sustainable agriculture development and facilitated access to agricultural inputs and equipments.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: GOAL Households can sustainably meet their basic needs and have improved coping strategies through strengthened livelihoods which place value on the natural environment. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Gender equality 2: this is the main objective of the outcome, which is aimed at addressing gender inequitable attitudes that reduce women’s access to health diets and safe drinking water.Aid to the environment 1: Capacity Building 1: This outcome establishes and trains Water Hygiene Sanitation Management Committees (COGEHA) within communities.Nutrition 1: This outcome includes nutrition education activities for behaviour change and adoption of good practices.
